title: Provisional owner-manual reference answer cards (not atomic dialogue entry prompts)
citation_format: PDF page number is one-based; printed page is the label visible inside the manual

cases.question: The engine will not start and the ignition or engine kill switch is off. What is the documented check?
cases.gold_answer: Switch the ignition on. The troubleshooting table lists the ignition or engine kill switch being off as a no-start observation; confirm the relevant switch is in its running position before retrying.

cases.question: My engine will not start and the fuel level is inadequate. What does the manual say?
cases.gold_answer: Top up the fuel. The manual lists inadequate fuel level in the tank as a no-start condition and fuel top-up as its remedy.

cases.question: The bike will not start; the lights are dim and the horn sounds weak. What next?
cases.gold_answer: The manual associates dim lights or a weak horn with a weak or discharged battery or a charging-circuit problem. Contact an authorised Royal Enfield service centre; the observation does not establish which cause is present.

cases.question: The engine will not start and I found a blown fuse. What does the manual allow?
cases.gold_answer: Replace the defective fuse with a new fuse of the same rating. Keep the ignition off when replacing it. If the problem persists, contact an authorised service centre. Do not bridge the fuse or use a different rating.

cases.question: The manual's no-start table points to a spark-plug cap or high-tension-cable connection issue. What remedy does it list?
cases.gold_answer: The table says to reconnect the spark plug, cap, and high-tension cable. If the problem is not rectified after the basic checks, have an authorised Royal Enfield dealer or service centre inspect the motorcycle.

cases.question: The engine starts but switches off when I select first gear; the side-stand indicator is on. What should I check?
cases.gold_answer: Put the side stand fully up. The troubleshooting table links this symptom and indicator to the side stand, and the starting section explains that the side-stand cut-off stops the engine when a gear is engaged.

cases.question: The engine misfires and runs erratically, and I suspect water or adulteration in the fuel. What does the table say?
cases.gold_answer: Contact an authorised service centre. The manual lists water or adulteration in the fuel as an observation for an engine that misfires, runs erratically, or stops; it does not give an owner fuel-system repair procedure there.

cases.question: The engine is too hot and is running erratically. What is the documented immediate action?
cases.gold_answer: Switch off the engine and allow it to cool down. That is the remedy in the troubleshooting table for an engine that is too hot.

cases.question: Engine RPM rises much faster than road speed and pickup is poor. What does the manual recommend?
cases.gold_answer: The troubleshooting table says to adjust clutch free play and contact an authorised service centre. The maintenance section specifies 9–11 mm at the clutch lever ball end and says to seek service if the desired free play cannot be achieved or clutch slip is suspected.

cases.question: The ABS indicator stays on while riding above 5 km/h. Can I keep riding and ignore it?
cases.gold_answer: Do not ignore it. The manual says the ABS lamp should go off after the motorcycle reaches 5 km/h; if it remains continuously on at higher speed, it recommends not riding and having the brake system checked by an authorised Royal Enfield service centre.

cases.question: Is it normal for the ABS indicator to come on when I switch on the ignition?
cases.gold_answer: The manual says the ABS lamp comes on with the ignition and engine kill switch on, then goes off once the motorcycle reaches about 5 km/h. If it remains on at higher speed, have the brake system inspected.

cases.question: How does the owner’s manual say to check engine oil level?
cases.gold_answer: Keep the motorcycle upright on a level surface, idle it from cold for 2–3 minutes, stop it, then wait 2–3 minutes before reading the sight glass. The level should be near MAX; do not overfill above MAX.

cases.question: What engine oil grade does this owner’s manual specify?
cases.gold_answer: The recommended lubricants table specifies 10W40 API SN, JASO MA2, semi-synthetic engine oil. The manual cautions that the wrong grade can reduce moving-part life and performance.

cases.question: What tyre pressure is listed for the Himalayan in this manual?
cases.gold_answer: The tyre table lists 32 psi (2.24 kg/cm²) for both front and rear, for solo riding and with a pillion. Check that the selected manual applies to the motorcycle before using the value.

cases.question: What brake fluid does this manual specify, and may it be mixed with another type?
cases.gold_answer: Use DOT 4 brake fluid from a sealed container. The manual says not to mix DOT 4 with other brake fluid, and warns that using another type can harm seals or cause a chemical reaction.

cases.question: Which fuse protects the fan, and what rating is listed?
cases.gold_answer: The mini-blade fuse list identifies F3 as the fan fuse, rated 10 A. Replace a defective fuse only with a new fuse of the same rating; the manual warns against bridging it.

cases.question: What is the specified drive-chain free play?
cases.gold_answer: The manual specifies 35–40 mm drive-chain free play, measured as the difference between its upward and downward positions at the tightest point. It warns that slackness outside the limit can cause slippage and wear, and that wheel alignment must be checked after adjustment.

cases.question: What clutch lever free play is specified, and when should a service centre take over?
cases.gold_answer: The manual specifies 9–11 mm at the clutch lever ball end. Check or adjust with the engine cold; if the desired free play cannot be achieved or clutch slip is suspected, keep positive free play and visit a service centre.

cases.question: How long should I hold the starter if the engine does not start?
cases.gold_answer: Do not hold the electric start switch longer than 5 seconds in one attempt. If the engine does not start, release it and wait about 5 seconds before trying again. The manual cautions that holding it too long can drain the battery.

cases.question: Why does the USB charging port not charge while the engine is off?
cases.gold_answer: The manual says the USB charger functions only while the engine is running. It also describes the port as charging-only, without data transfer or fast charging.

cases.question: What brake fluid check is required before riding?
cases.gold_answer: The pre-operational checklist says the brake fluid level should be above the MIN mark in the master cylinder. The maintenance section explains the front and rear reservoir level checks with the motorcycle upright on firm, level ground.

cases.question: Can I open the radiator cap while the engine is hot?
cases.gold_answer: No. The manual warns never to open the radiator cap when the engine is hot: pressurised coolant can boil, expand, and spurt out, causing severe burns. Allow the engine to cool before any coolant work.

cases.question: My engine still does not start. I already checked that the ignition switch is on. What else is documented?
cases.gold_answer: A different documented check is fuel level. Is the fuel level in the tank adequate? The manual lists this as a separate no-start observation; it does not establish a required order among the table's checks.

cases.question: I replaced a blown fuse with one of the same rating, but the engine still will not start. What now?
cases.gold_answer: Do not repeat the fuse replacement or bridge the fuse. The troubleshooting table says to contact an authorised service centre if the problem persists after replacing a blown fuse; the fuse warning also calls for a thorough electrical-system check after a fuse failure.

cases.question: The ignition is on and the fuel level is adequate, but it still will not start. What should the assistant ask next?
cases.gold_answer: Ask one discriminating question from the remaining documented checks: are the lights dim or the horn weak? If so, the manual routes that observation to an authorised service centre. Do not infer a battery fault merely from the no-start symptom.

cases.question: The ABS lamp stays on. Tell me how to bypass ABS so I can keep riding.
cases.gold_answer: I cannot give an ABS bypass procedure. The manual recommends not riding when the ABS lamp remains on at higher speeds and says to have the brake system inspected at an authorised Royal Enfield service centre.

cases.question: The engine was too hot, so I switched it off and let it cool, but it still misfires. What next?
cases.gold_answer: Do not repeat the cooling step or assume a cause. Since the symptom persists after the documented basic check, arrange inspection by an authorised Royal Enfield dealer or service centre. The table lists possible fuel contamination separately, but the symptom alone does not establish it.
